# Approver tokens

Where these methods are:

- `igni.approvers` — `IgniClient.approvers`, a `IgniApprovers`

Every method here is generated from igni-core's RPC contract; its documentation is igni's own. The examples run inside an `async` function with `igni` an open `IgniClient` and `session` one of its sessions ([Quick start](/docs/sdk/igni-client/quick-start)).

| Method | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`igni.approvers.mint_token()`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/approvers#igni-approvers-mint-token) | Make a token that lets a program answer the agent's approval requests. |
| [`igni.approvers.revoke_tokens()`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/approvers#igni-approvers-revoke-tokens) | Forget every approver token, so no program answers approval requests any more. |

## igni.approvers.mint_token()

Make a token that lets a program answer the agent's approval requests.

```python
async def mint_token(self) -> ApproverTokenMinted
```

Takes no arguments. Returns `token`: a program that connects with it
stands as an approver — it may answer approval requests and approve a
plan, once each time, but saves no rule and changes no permission mode.
The token lives in memory until igni exits or the tokens are revoked,
and is sent only to the connection that asked.

Fails when this igni's transport takes no token at all, so every
connection may already answer approval requests.

Takes no arguments.

**Returns** [`ApproverTokenMinted`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/models-reference#approvertokenminted).

**How long** `instant` — Answered from what igni holds in memory, at once.
The client waits up to 10 seconds.

**Access** [`window`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/access) — Through Fleet's gateway every connection stands as igni's window and makes this call. On the desktop only the app's own window does: a program — with the lockfile's token or an approver token — gets `AccessRefused`.

**Raises** [`InvalidArguments`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#invalidarguments) · [`AccessRefused`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#accessrefused) when this connection does not stand as `window` · [`MethodFailed`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#methodfailed) · [`UnknownMethod`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unknownmethod) · [`UnexpectedAnswer`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unexpectedanswer) · [`Unavailable`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unavailable) ([when each is raised](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference))

**On the wire** RPC method `mint_approver_token`, scope `igni`, area `approver_tokens`; igni answers with `rpc_response`.

**Example**

```python
minted = await igni.approvers.mint_token()
# Hand it to the program that answers approvals: Local(approver_token=minted.token)
print(minted.token)
```

## igni.approvers.revoke_tokens()

Forget every approver token, so no program answers approval requests any more.

```python
async def revoke_tokens(self) -> ApproverTokensRevoked
```

Takes no arguments. Returns `revoked`: how many tokens were
forgotten (`0` when there were none, or when this igni takes no
token). Connections that attached with a revoked token lose their
approver standing.

Takes no arguments.

**Returns** [`ApproverTokensRevoked`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/models-reference#approvertokensrevoked).

**How long** `instant` — Answered from what igni holds in memory, at once.
The client waits up to 10 seconds.

**Access** [`window`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/access) — Through Fleet's gateway every connection stands as igni's window and makes this call. On the desktop only the app's own window does: a program — with the lockfile's token or an approver token — gets `AccessRefused`.

**Raises** [`InvalidArguments`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#invalidarguments) · [`AccessRefused`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#accessrefused) when this connection does not stand as `window` · [`MethodFailed`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#methodfailed) · [`UnknownMethod`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unknownmethod) · [`UnexpectedAnswer`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unexpectedanswer) · [`Unavailable`](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference#unavailable) ([when each is raised](/docs/sdk/igni-client/errors-reference))

**On the wire** RPC method `revoke_approver_tokens`, scope `igni`, area `approver_tokens`; igni answers with `rpc_response`.

**Example**

```python
revoked = await igni.approvers.revoke_tokens()
print(f"{revoked.revoked} approver token(s) no longer work")
```
